title: AI, Risk, and the Future of Systematic Investing - Systematic Investor - Ep.387

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/AI, Risk, and the Future of Systematic Investing - Systematic Investor - Ep.387.docx

speakers: Andrew Beer (co-host, DBi / DBMF managed-futures replication ETF)
Tom Roble (co-host, SG CTA/Trend index research; captioned name)
Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host, Top Traders Unplugged; captioned 'Neil's Krup Larson')
summary: Top Traders Unplugged Systematic Investor Ep.387 (Feb 2026): Beer, Roble and Kaastrup-Larsen review 2025-26 trend-following performance (gold, non-US equities, April 2025 deleveraging), debate short- vs long-term models and risk management, and critique liquid alternatives, replication and QIS products. Main conclusions: long-term models paid, short-term models were a costly risk tool, CTA alpha is being early contrarian and right, and many liquid-alt products fail because they are sold not bought.

Roble on shift away from US dollar/US exceptionalism; euro investor S&P return; Olympics chatter
Olympics chatter; Google 100-year bond; Rasmussen on why hedge funds improved vs private equity

2025 familiar trend year; risk allocation, longer-term models, manager dispersion, silver risk, overextension models
Gold up 60% yet CTA space flat; short-term models detracted; short-term trend as costly risk management; April deleveraging
Dynamic position sizing vs static; stop execution gap risk; market count dilution; concentrated CTAs hard to sell
Role of CTA vs multistrat; what is CTA alpha (early contrarian); noise vs information-driven trends
Short vs long models; zero-Sharpe short-term trend; local traders exploit CTA de-risking; non-core positions
Short-term models in April drawdown; allocator fear of whipsaw; liquid alts poor results; product development

Risk premia narrative history; manager risk in trend; allocators combining flavours; outlook and sign-off
Housekeeping, sign-off and sponsor reads

completeness_estimate: 0.87 - good coverage of the main threads; missed 2025 sector attribution (gold/non-US equities, poor bonds, short JGBs), CTA VaR mix, replication tracking variance, rebalance speed in V-reversals, track-record length, equity long-short fee math and the don't-time-trend advice; two speaker errors.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: I believe that that is actually going to be very very positive for for for trend falling we need real economic change to to make money
claims.claim: AI-driven economic disruption should be positive for trend following because trend strategies need real change in the economy to profit.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: I don't think asset allocators are going to say uh you know what let's have AI pick the next hedge fund for me.
claims.claim: Asset management remains a people business, so allocators will not hand manager selection to AI, though AI will help average allocators become more sophisticated.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it actually did say all right if you want to achieve these investment objectives it it you know it brought managed futures as one of the core um elements of doing that
claims.claim: AI asset-allocation analyses recommend managed futures as a core element, suggesting spreading knowledge will increase allocations to trend.
claims.indicator: managed futures allocation in AI-generated portfolios

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: the perception as investors is that the period of US exceptionalism is is maybe over
claims.claim: After 2025 non-US investors see higher US risk and are rethinking US asset exposure, though not wholesale selling.
claims.indicator: US dollar and US assets for foreign investors

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: a euro investor uh with the same S&P 500 investment was up just 2 and a half% last year
claims.claim: Dollar weakness cut a euro investor's 2025 S&P 500 return to about 2.5% versus 16% in USD, so currency exposure dominates foreign returns.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: normally you have non-American investors can rely on the US dollar to rise in times of stress and the US dollar has enjoyed the status of being a safe haven currency
claims.claim: The dollar's safe-haven status weakened in 2025, removing the usual hedge for non-US holders of US assets.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: global equity markets don't have the capacity for a wholesale shift in in investor assets away from the US
claims.claim: Global equity markets are too small to absorb a wholesale reallocation from the US, so the shift is limited to specific parts of US risk.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: apparently has not happened since 1997 where Motorola issued a 100red-year bond
claims.claim: Google issuing a 100-year bond is rare (last in 1997 by Motorola) and may say something about duration expectations.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: hedge funds in his view simply had to improve because of the competition and the attention that private equity was given um by by investors for so long
claims.claim: Hedge funds improved managers, structures and processes under competition and mark-to-market discipline while private equity merely grew bigger.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: they would overcommit to it with the expectation that they would get money back in a certain period of time
claims.claim: Allocators overcommitted to private equity expecting distributions that did not arrive, creating over-exposure and driving the secondaries market and renewed hedge fund interest.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the return characteristic of private equity essentially being some version of leverage equity
claims.claim: Private equity is essentially leveraged equity with smoothed marks, which is less attractive when equity valuations are high and expected 10-year returns low.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the attitude used to be FOMO about the US markets and now has has has come to people saying like, well, wait a second
claims.claim: The attitude to US markets has shifted from FOMO to concern about predictability and rule of law, drawing attention to hedge funds that can make money in this environment.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: We've got stubborn inflation. We've got geopolitical dislocations and tensions.
claims.claim: Stubborn inflation, geopolitics, commodities returning from compressed volatility and rates higher than recent history make the environment better for long-short tactical global macro.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my own trend barometer finished yesterday at 50 and that's still a pretty productive environment for trend following
claims.claim: The host's trend barometer at 50 indicates a productive and consistent trend environment in Feb 2026.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Stocken trend index up 1.65% uh for the month, up 6.43% for the year.
claims.claim: SG Trend Index was up 6.43% YTD to mid-Feb 2026 and S&P 500 about 1.5%, so trend outperformed equities.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: on average last year the zed scores so the opportunity sets is similar to your kind of barometer I think uh was pretty poor
claims.claim: In 2025 average breakout z-scores across about 200-500 parameters were poor, so risk allocation to the few trending markets (metals) decided performance.
claims.indicator: breakout model z-scores across parameters and markets
claims.conditions: when breadth of trends is low

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: in 2025, it's really been the precious metals that have been the key performance drivers
claims.claim: Commodities drove trend profits two years running but from different sources: softs and metals in 2024, precious metals in 2025.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: we're seeing really good trending markets in Cosby, Niki, the Swedish OMX, and IBEX 35
claims.claim: In early 2026 smaller equity indices (Kospi, Nikkei, OMX, IBEX 35) show the best trends, so market selection matters.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: CTAs generate alpha when they're early contrarian and right.
claims.claim: CTA alpha comes from being early, contrarian and right, e.g. adding equity risk and keeping gold after Liberation Day.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: human strategists after liberation day were really rattled and really wrong
claims.claim: Human strategists feared recession after Liberation Day; CTAs, which do not care about narratives, rode the rebound and kept positions.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: people have been talking about a fundamentally driven rotation into non- US equities for 15 years and it hasn't worked
claims.claim: Fundamental rotation to non-US equities failed for 15 years but has finally occurred in the last couple of years, which trend captured.
claims.indicator: non-US vs US equity relative performance

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: gold was a failed trade for a decade and a half
claims.claim: Gold failed for 15 years and did not rise in 2022 when expected, then soared from 2024 for different reasons, showing narratives mislead and trend works.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the leadership has changed a little bit in February. It's not so much medals uh anymore.
claims.claim: In Feb 2026 trend leadership rotated from metals to equities, natural gas and currencies.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Yet from a trend following perspective, it was a very familiar year. Few markets did all the heavy lifting.
claims.claim: In 2025 trend followers saw the usual pattern of a few big winners and several small losers despite unusual events.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: we normally see a much stronger preference for longerterm models outperforming
claims.claim: Longer-term trend models normally outperform shorter-term ones (speed factor); 2025 followed that.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: it's really the allocation of risk last year that was the key thing and how you managed that risk.
claims.claim: With few trending markets in 2025, risk allocation and risk management decided manager returns.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: we still got many managers in that 10 to 15% range
claims.claim: Manager returns in early 2026 ranged about 8-15% YTD, showing good risk management.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: please ask us for the data on the SG trend indicator, which is our hypothetical model-based portfolio, which with with very limited u risk management, and you'll see some very interesting swings in the precious metals markets
claims.claim: Unmanaged trend portfolios swing heavily in precious metals, while actual CTAs cut risk quickly during the late-January 2026 selloff.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: silver has caught a lot of headlines but it's not as big a market as gold and so maybe the allocation of risk to that market wasn't as big
claims.claim: Silver risk allocation in CTAs was small relative to gold because it is a smaller market.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: we've had CTAs kind of building proprietary models over the years to help them work out when trends are overextended
claims.claim: CTAs use proprietary trend-strength and overextension models to size down late in trends.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: gold is up 60%. Right? I mean I mean this should have been a banner year for the space
claims.claim: In 2025 gold rose 60% and equities rallied yet the CTA space was flat, because short-term models detracted.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you're up 20% or something in in in long-term trend according to that and you're down you know 12, 13, 14, 15 and short-term trend
claims.claim: In SG's trend-indicator factor analysis long-term trend returned about +20% in 2025 while short-term trend lost 12-15%.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: they're a riskmanagement tool and they're often a costly risk management tool
claims.claim: Short-term trend models have no strong Sharpe and are costly risk management tools that raise trading costs.
claims.direction: avoid large risk to short-term models

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: If you're going to allocate a meaningful amount of money to something that has a zero sharp ratio over time
claims.claim: Allocating risk to a zero-Sharpe component to reduce volatility is a poor trade.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it really was all about the April uh deleveraging thanks to liberation day
claims.claim: Trend profits in 2025 equities were limited because April deleveraging forced cuts and some managers went short before the rebound.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: even though we made most money in in precious metals, we were selling precious metals all year, right?
claims.claim: A modern trend follower with variable position sizing sold precious metals as volatility rose, giving up some profit.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you may trigger your signal you may trigger your stop but you may not execute that trade until the next day
claims.claim: Stops triggered on Friday execute Monday, so weekend-style gaps can destroy managers who do not cut risk with volatility.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they often trade three four 500 markets. And therefore any one market even if you don't touch your position size becomes a very small risk allocation in reality
claims.claim: Managers with static positions and hundreds of markets get little from outliers; to make 50-80% returns you need few markets and a large risk allocation.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if you really want to have punchy returns and make those 50 60 80% returns yeah then you actually have to have a fairly small set of markets
claims.claim: Concentrated trend programs create return but are hard to sell given investment committee constraints and strategic allocations.

correction.issue: Likely wrong speaker: the 'London CTA manager... difficult to sell to investors' remark is Tom Roble's; Niels replies 'you don't need many investors'.
correction.fix: Tom Roble: concentrated trend programs create return but are hard to sell given investment committee constraints and strategic allocations.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: trend following is really good at diversifying that and so the investors sort of continued fascination with multistrat isn't necessarily meeting the requirements
claims.claim: Investors whose core risk is equities want asymmetric diversification, which trend delivers better than multi-strategy funds.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: The valuable trends for CTAs are when it's something's at 10, fair market value is 10, and then the information changes.
claims.claim: Valuable trends occur when fair value changes and informed participants like the asset more at each higher price.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the smart money selling at 11, buying at 9, selling at 11, buying at 9
claims.claim: Sentiment-driven oscillation without change in fundamental value is noise captured by locals and high-frequency traders, while trend followers get whipsawed.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: they waited for the day when CTAs when some signal went off somewhere and CTAs were selling
claims.claim: Fundamental commodity traders waited for CTA signals to trigger selling and bought from them, a cost for CTAs.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the shorter term models are the ones that are going to get whipssawed violently when you have these changes in sentiment like we had last year
claims.claim: Short-term models are whipsawed by sentiment shifts without real change in the state of the world, while long-term models capture lasting shifts such as the move out of US assets.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: if you're going to introduce something into your into your portfolio and allocate a lot of risk to something with a zero sharp ratio, no thanks
claims.claim: Risk management should not be conflated with allocating heavily to a zero-Sharpe strategy.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you're not executing at at you know there the liquidity dries up in that market because they can see you coming
claims.claim: When CTAs de-risk after a vol spike, local traders in that market trade against them, so CTAs pay implementation costs and liquidity dries up.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: this diversification into a lot of excess positions, you know, non increasingly non-core positions, I think it hurt people after liberation day
claims.claim: Adding many non-core markets increases drawdowns during de-risking because of implementation costs.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: when you're building these models, you have to make certain assumptions about implementation costs and I don't think most people factor in um uh getting taken advantage of by local traders
claims.claim: Backtests understate costs because they ignore being picked off by local traders.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: really short-term models were fine during that you know they actually they they actually preserved capital much better than longerterm guys
claims.claim: In the initial April 2025 shock short-term models preserved capital better than long-term ones; they lost later in chop.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: investor preferences are often to live in paralyzing fear about what a bad lipsaw looks like
claims.claim: Allocators fear the bad whipsaw and a Friday loss turning into a worse Monday, but paying for protection costs too much.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: let's do a long-term trend model and then and then buy out of the money puts on equities because that's what we're afraid of
claims.claim: Hedging a long-term trend model with out-of-the-money puts out of fear of tail events is a losing business.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: The returns over 15 years according to Wilshire's data is between two and 3%. And the fee structures on average is about 200 basis points
claims.claim: Liquid alternative funds returned 2-3% over 15 years with about 200 bp fees while equities rose about 14% a year.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: a typical firm has a huge distribution infrastructure to support and they have no view on which is the best product that they're going to launch
claims.claim: Liquid-alt products are launched to feed distribution rather than from investment conviction, which explains poor outcomes.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: most products that are developed in the space are developed by sales people who think they can sell it over the next year or two
claims.claim: Products designed by salespeople to meet demand rather than investment merit, like a car designed by the showroom salesman, fail investors.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: are we talking about real hedge funds in that data or are we talking about quasi alternatives
claims.claim: Liquid-alt category data may mix true hedge funds with quasi multi-asset funds labelled multi-strat, so classification matters.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: strategies that become scalable that form part of a larger longer term tactical asset allocation that you want to have as a core holding like a CTA
claims.claim: Hedge fund industry splits into scalable strategies forming part of tactical asset allocation (like CTAs, with falling costs) and pure alpha that goes in and out of vogue.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: even Blackstone gave up on that you know I mean Newberg Burman shut down their fault like it was a failed business model
claims.claim: Multi-manager mutual fund and ETF products failed as a business model.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: I kept asking these questions like what's the realized sharp ratio of the strategy for over what period of time and what do you think it's going to be be going forward and why?
claims.claim: QIS/premium providers talk about engineering and research, not realised Sharpe ratios, so due diligence should ask for realised Sharpe over a stated period.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: get very very clear about what you're expecting a product to do and how you're expecting to achieve to achieve it
claims.claim: Allocators should define the signal they want and implement it efficiently, not pick managers by narrative.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I feel at least that the tracking error to the index that it's trying to mirror is too large for that
claims.claim: A replication ETF has large tracking error to the index, so it is better viewed as an alternative-data trend strategy than as a cost saving.
claims.indicator: tracking error of replication vs SG CTA index

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: Okay, that's a top quartortile maybe a top decile hedge fund portfolio over time.
claims.claim: Standard Life GARS promised equity beta 0.2 with cash plus 5, a top-decile hedge fund result, and was unrealistic though it reached $90 billion.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: G10 currency carry does not have a long-term sharp ratio 1.2. I'm sorry that's that's a back test.
claims.claim: Risk premia backtests overstate Sharpe (G10 carry 1.2); live results drop about 75% from backtest.
claims.indicator: G10 carry Sharpe in backtest vs live

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: something like 75% or something
claims.claim: Backtested to live performance decay of risk premia products is about 75%.

correction.issue: Duplicate of MT013-C16-3 (same 75% backtest-to-live decay point).
correction.fix: Merge into MT013-C16-3: risk premia backtests overstate Sharpe (G10 carry 1.2); live results fall about 75% short of backtests.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: a mutual fund that tries to pick six underlying hedge fund managers and hires them in managed accounts is not going to achieve the return objectives
claims.claim: A multi-manager mutual fund of hedge fund managers cannot achieve the promised return objectives after costs and constraints.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: most alternative liquid alternative products are sold not bought.
claims.claim: Capital flows to the largest firms with the largest sales forces, not to the best products.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the reason AQR went to 14 billion in assets in their mutual fund was because a lot of allocators were basically saying it's AQR a it's AQR what can go wrong
claims.claim: Allocators with line-item limits chose AQR for brand, taking idiosyncratic manager risk they did not understand.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: global macro hedge funds who want to access some sort of curve steepener or some sort of thematic play for a finite period of time who will use the QIS
claims.claim: Macro funds use bank QIS indices for thematic bets like curve steepeners, outsourcing execution and financing.

correction.issue: Wrong speaker: 'SG has a very active QIS business... often we have global macro hedge funds who want to access some sort of curve steepener' is Tom Roble (SG), not the host.
correction.fix: Tom Roble: macro funds use bank QIS indices for thematic bets like curve steepeners, outsourcing execution and financing.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: lowcost ETF model portfolios that that that require things that are look and feel more betalike
claims.claim: Low-cost ETF model portfolios create a market for beta-like alternative indices at low fees.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: have no transparency. We have no idea what the returns actually are.
claims.claim: QIS trend-replication products do not publish returns, so cannot be evaluated.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: when you do things really differently why would you expect to be able to deliver the same outcome
claims.claim: Replication using different methods may not deliver the CTA outcome in all regimes; the last 10 years differ from the first 10 of this millennium.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: when did you actually launch this index right if you if you launched the index three weeks ago then have you launched other indices that look like this how did those do right
claims.claim: Due diligence on bank trend indices should ask when launched and how prior similar indices performed, as many allocators suspended belief.
claims.indicator: index launch date and track record

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: risk premium implies that if the three of us design it, it's going to look the same
claims.claim: Calling trend a risk premium is misleading because different designers' trend indices differ greatly.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: we're just harvesting risk premia that have been around for 70 years and these are permanent features of the market
claims.claim: After 2007 quant losses the narrative shifted to risk-premia harvesting as permanent, which understated risk.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: manager risk as we talk about is very very high in this space
claims.claim: Two long-term trend models with correlation 0.8 can still be 20 points apart in a year, so manager risk is high.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: how as an investor how how is an allocator do I want to put these together into a package thereby becoming almost like an outsourced uh uh portfolio manager
claims.claim: Sophisticated allocators now combine several banks' flavours of trend to diversify design risk.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: maybe this could be a good year for us
claims.claim: Strategies that do not predict but profit from change may do well in 2026 given the amount going on in the world.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: being you know up to their gills and things like software stocks that could be disrupted
claims.claim: Allocators are heavily exposed through private equity to software companies that AI could disrupt, adding to the case against long-term leveraged long equity exposure.
claims.direction: PE/software valuations down if AI disrupts
claims.conditions: high equity valuations and AI disruption
claims.testable: partly - PE software exposure vs subsequent marks

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: In fact you bonds was really poor last year.
claims.claim: Bond markets offered poor trend opportunities for CTAs in 2025.
claims.indicator: breakout-model z-scores in bond futures (SG trend indicator)
claims.testable: yes - trend returns by sector in 2025

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: I looked at a CTA report today and there was a much bigger allocation of VAR to equities and FX.
claims.claim: Despite the headlines, CTAs had less risk in precious metals than assumed; their VaR allocation was much larger in equities and FX.
claims.conditions: early 2026, after the precious metals selloff

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it was making money in gold and non- US equities um was about about half the performance each and then you got whipsaw and and hope you didn't lose too much money in in rates and currencies
claims.claim: In 2025 trend gains came roughly half from gold and half from non-US equities, while rates and currencies produced whipsaw losses.
claims.testable: yes - sector attribution of CTA indices

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a couple of them also in the say short JTBs
claims.claim: Most 2025 trend profits came from metals or select equities, with short Japanese government bonds (JGBs) another profitable trend.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: You know, in 2023, they all went against us and we underperformed by 500 basis points.
claims.claim: A futures-based CTA replication can deviate from the hedge funds it tracks by several hundred bp a year (about -500 bp in 2023, large outperformance in 2024-2025), driven by about four sources of variation.
claims.indicator: replication tracking difference vs SG CTA index
claims.testable: yes - annual tracking difference of replication ETFs vs index

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: we were slow to derisk and and balanced when Trump Trump changed his mind.
claims.claim: Slow (weekly) de-risking helped around Liberation Day because the sell-off reversed quickly; faster de-risking sold near the low.
claims.conditions: sharp policy-driven sell-offs that reverse quickly (V-shaped)
claims.testable: yes - compare trend models by rebalance speed in V-shaped reversals

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Even if you have 5 years of underperformance doesn't mean the next 5 years, the next 10 years won't
claims.claim: Strategies go in and out of favour, so 5-10 years of track record says little about the next 5-10 years; past underperformance does not predict future underperformance.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: equity long short as a as a category if you have a beta of 0.5 or point4 to equities it it's not going to the amount of stock selection alpha and other things you need to do
claims.claim: Equity long-short funds with 0.4-0.5 equity beta need more stock-selection alpha than is realistic to overcome mutual fund costs, so they are unlikely to add value.
claims.conditions: in mutual fund/liquid alt wrappers with high fees

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: very few allocators actively trade which they should I tell them if you're going to actively trade you you find something else to trade.
claims.claim: Managed futures exposure should be held as a core allocation, not traded tactically; allocators who want to time something should time another asset.
claims.testable: partly - investor flow timing vs buy-and-hold returns of trend funds
